messages.author: 1cf31f7ec35affd4
messages.subject: heatmap with two color ranges
parts:
Hello,

I am attempting to make a heatmap, but I want to use two color ranges
to represent the sign of the value of interest. I've used the code
below to produce a regular heatmap with one color range. I would like
to modify it so that if the value of 'Error' is negative, then I use
scale_fill_gradient(low='red', high='white'), and if the value of
'Error' is positive, then I would use
scale_fill_gradient(low='white' , high='blue').

If I just use two scale_fill_gradient statements with non-overlapping
ranges, the second over-writes the first. And unfortunately simply
using a color range of red to blue doesn't give me the distinction
between positive and negative values that I would like to have. I've
also tinkered with using if then statements, but haven't found a
solution. Any ideas how to go about this?

Thanks for your help!

Best,
Jake

dat=read.csv('file_path')

(p=ggplot(dat, aes(Base_Ne, Birth_Rate)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=Error),
colour="black") + scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high="blue", breaks
= seq(min(-10), max(80), length.out = 10)))

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: heatmap with two color ranges
parts:
It is my understanding that you will never get two color scales on the same plot. 

Have you tried scale_fill_gradient2? 
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/scale_gradient2.html

Should be able to set the midpoint at 0 = white and do your red and blue from there. 

B
